product: Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read the appliance syslog of BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support: a BG header, then field=value pairs separated by semicolons. The appliances send it to the data collector. Logins, access console logouts and password changes go to Auth, and every other event goes to ManagementEvent.
notes:
Setup:
- BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support appliances write the same syslog format: a BG header with a site ID and segment numbers, then field=value pairs separated by semicolons.
- Send the syslog from /appliance > Security > Appliance Administration > Syslog to the data collector.

Field mapping:
- Logins (with the failure reason), access console logouts and password changes go to Auth; every other event (users, settings, policies, vault accounts and password rotations) goes to ManagementEvent with the whole field list in operation.
- Messages over 1 KB arrive as segments and stay in the generic schema.
- BeyondTrust doesn't quote values, so the parent gives SPLIT_NAME_VALUES the backslash, which BeyondTrust escapes, as the quote character.
- With " as the quote character, a lone " in a value, such as 27" in a display name, made the studio's emulator join the fields after it, which Sophos NG-SIEM doesn't.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the examples on BeyondTrust's message format pages with made-up values.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (116 of 116 fields matched the emulator, including a value with an escaped semicolon and the three header variants), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 9 Run Tests.
- In Run Test on 2026-10-16 all 130 fields matched the emulator, a quoted value with an escaped = included.

Known gaps:
- A line doesn't say whether PRA or RS sent it.
- Session activity (session start and end, file transfer, shell) isn't in the appliance syslog; BeyondTrust sends it through its Middleware Engine SIEM Tool plugin, which this entry doesn't cover.
